text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Some 10,000 junior doctors demonstrated in Paris yesterday against planned tightening of government controls of health spending.
-- Seita cigarette manufacturer worried by a possible price cut trend in France.
-- Arms procurement agency DGA chairman Jean-Yves Helmer says in an interview the French arms co-operation programs have been affected by cuts in military budgets throughout Europe.

-- Suez and Lyonnaise des Eaux may pay a heavy price for their planned merger, as Suez shareholders call for an exceptional dividend worth a few billion francs. Belgian businessman Albert Frere may increase his stake in Societe Generale de Belgique.
-- Club Mediterranee to sell its cruising yachts for up to 400 million francs.

-- PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet in an interview says he worries over a "bad euro", in which Italy, Spain and Portugal would not be part of the first wave of monetary union, and calls for better protection for European industrialists against imports.
-- Air Inter Europe to strike on Monday and Tuesday, to protest conditions of a planned merger with Air France.
-- Junior doctors to meet with Health Minister Jacques Barrot over planned government controls of health spending.
-- Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer may agree to delay planned plant shut down in Belgium by a few weeks.
-- Bordeaux courts blocks sale of part of Chateau d'Yquem vineyard to luxury goods conglomerate LVMH at the request of one of the owners.
